🇺🇸🇮🇷 US enforces a blockade of Iranian ports, citing 'severe' threat
The US has announced military operations to enforce a blockade across the Persian Gulf, the Strait of Hormuz, the Gulf of Oman, and the Arabian Sea, targeting Iran. It applies to all vessels, regardless of their flag or ownership.
The regional threat level has been raised to “severe.”
🗣 “Neutral vessels carrying neutral cargo or sailing in ballast between neutral ports in the Gulf of Oman and the Strait of Hormuz may be subject to questioning, visits, and searches to confirm their intentions regarding the blockade,” the Joint Maritime Information Center (JMIC) said in its announcement.
The JMIC urges ships to keep monitoring VHF Channel 16 and follow all instructions from US forces.
The US first imposed its naval blockade targeting Iranian ports and shipping on April 13. It was temporarily lifted on June 18 but reinstated on July 14.

🇮🇷🇮🇱 Israel poses a persistent risk to global energy markets – Iranian foreign minister
Abbas Araghchi has warned that possible Israeli-instigated military misadventures in the Persian Gulf region remain a threat for both gas suppliers and consumers.
The US and Israel have recently raised the [prospect of renewed attacks](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/76921) on Iran, with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu claiming that Israel has an opportunity [to eliminate the “existential threat”](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/76907) posed by Iran in cooperation with the US, according to The Times of Israel.
Meanwhile, the outcome of the Israeli general election remains unclear. Although Netanyahu's bloc appears to be leading over that of his rival, Gadi Eisenkot, neither side has yet secured the 61 seats needed for[ a parliamentary majority](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/76892).
Araghchi's remarks come in the wake of the 8th Summit of Heads of State and Government of the Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF) in Moscow and talks held this week in Tehran with senior officials from Iran, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkey.
Previously, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian announced shared understandings with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Emir of Qatar Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani on cooperation in agriculture, oil and gas, road construction, security, and bilateral relations, according to the Tasnim News Agency.

🛢 Gulf states push for Hormuz reopening and wider Iran-US deal
A multipronged peace deal is taking shape at the heart of Gulf states' plans to avert what they see as a disastrous renewal of war between Iran and the US, The Guardian reports.
The terms under discussion: the Strait of Hormuz would reopen within four days of sanctions being lifted — Iran has reportedly cut its original proposal from seven days to four — while the Houthis would withdraw substantial forces inside Yemen.
Iran is also reportedly acknowledging a mediating role in Yemen, with security council secretary Mohsen Rezaei meeting the Houthi ambassador on Tuesday.
The sticking point is Washington's demand, backed by European powers, that Iran readmit UN weapons inspectors to its nuclear sites. Tehran has refused, saying it will only hold talks in principle on its nuclear program. Instead, Iran kept the nuclear file off the agenda at the Tehran meeting with Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan, focusing on a long-term regional security vision that would include the Gulf states and see the US military presence reduced or ended.

events.text:
🇸🇦 Regional war threatens to derail Saudi Arabia’s economic makeover
Iranian strikes and a renewed Houthi offensive are hitting Saudi Arabia on multiple fronts, putting its economic ambitions at risk, the Cradle reports.
The damage is becoming increasingly difficult to contain:
🔴 Attacks on the Manifa and Khurais oilfields reportedly cut production by around 600,000 barrels per day, while strikes on the East–West Pipeline disrupted a critical route for exporting crude through the Red Sea
🔴 Saudi Arabia’s aviation sector also took a hit after around 45% of scheduled flights were canceled between October 8 and 25, with cancellations at Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport reaching approximately 86%
🔴 The economic strain is mounting as the Saudi stock market fell 2.7% on October 25, its steepest single-session drop in 18 months, while the projected 2026 budget deficit rose to around 245 billion riyals
🔴 Prolonged regional instability threatens investor confidence and could delay major projects central to Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman’s Vision 2030 plan to diversify Saudi Arabia’s economy
Riyadh now faces a difficult choice between escalating its confrontation with the Houthis and pursuing a political settlement with Sanaa. Neither continuing the conflict nor the concessions required for peace comes without a cost.

🇮🇷🇺🇸 US burns through $47B in Iran war - report
The final bill could climb even higher with the US military now staring down the cost of replacing lost weapons and equipment, Reuters reports, citing Department of War data.
The breakdown shows exactly where much of the money is heading:
🔴 More than $29 billion is projected to replace munitions used during the conflict
🔴 Over $6 billion will be needed to replace military equipment and losses, including aircraft and drones
🔴 The total has surged from $25 billion in late April to $37.5 billion in July before surpassing $47 billion in the latest Pentagon estimate
The bombs may have stopped falling, but the bill keeps climbing.
